claude.rationale: The slice documents a whole-company reverse triangular merger in which Capital Bank Financial and its operating bank subsidiary (Capital Bank Corporation) were absorbed entirely into First Horizon and First Tennessee Bank National Association — the customer-facing banking franchise (T4) and the operations/charter that produce it (T5) were consolidated together via the bank merger into the acquirer's existing bank subsidiary, so product and process moved as one integrated unit (gap_45=0). Because the entire operating bank charter merged into First Tennessee alongside a governance bridge (two former directors, including the Chairman/CEO, joining the First Horizon board under a superseding employment agreement, plus contractually addressed executive severance/employment terms), the process consolidation was not documented as severed from its people/organization at closing (gap_56=0). No Tier-1 fusion (founder-as-product or person-as-legal-subject) is documented; this is a corporate absorption with controlling intent replaced by First Horizon's.

gemini.rationale: The transaction was a whole-company merger where Capital Bank Financial and its bank subsidiary were merged into First Horizon and its bank subsidiary. There is no evidence of a structural mismatch between the product (T4) and process (T5) layers, nor between the process (T5) and organization (T6) layers, as the entire entity and its operations were absorbed together.

openai.rationale: The whole acquired company and its operating bank were absorbed into First Horizon and First Tennessee Bank, with the acquired bank's charter and operations consolidated together; the slice documents no separation of customer-facing products from their operating processes at closing. The employment and severance arrangements were not identified as a transitional-services or operating agreement allocating a shared operational substrate.
